errors.quote: A triple $T$ has indicator $t_T$ with $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S∩T|-1$ ... and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$. So each line $\langle t_T\rangle$ is nondegenerate, and neighbors' lines are orthogonal.
errors.problem: The page states this right after defining both forms, with no qualifier, but it holds only for the rational form x^T(I-J/9)y. For the F_2 dot product of the phase network, t_S.t_T=|S cap T| mod 2 and t_T.t_T=1. Read literally, <t_T,t_T>=2=0 in F_2 makes each line isotropic (degenerate), and |S cap T|-1 is odd for the complex neighbors (even intersection), so they would not be orthogonal. The paper treats the two cases separately: 'For the complex network, take instead F=F_2^h with the ordinary dot product; here t_T.t_T=1.'

errors.quote: A nonzero residual contains a coordinate unit vector, hence an orthonormal basis
errors.problem: This is false. For example, the side 5->7 residual P(x)<t_Y>(x)Q is a line spanned by a tensor of three triple indicators (weight 27), and the center residual P(x)F(x)Q contains no coordinate unit of F^{otimes3} when P or Q is spanned by a vector of weight above one. The inference also skips nondegeneracy. The paper shows each residual is nondegenerate and contains a norm-one vector, made by tensoring coordinate units (in B, Q^perp, triple complements, full spaces) with the norm-one vectors spanning P and Q. It then uses the fact that a nondegenerate nonalternating binary space has an orthonormal basis.
The paper uses the normalized H=(1/sqrt2)[[1,1],[1,-1]]. With the unnormalized Hadamard matrix the product is 2(aI+bX), and H diag(1,-1)H=2X, so C_U would be off by 2^m.

errors.quote: Outgoing labels $A\otimes F$ on $X$ and $B'$ on $Y$ equal the next incoming ones
errors.problem: The page never introduces the one-dimensional factor Q=<t_{a_{j+1}} (x)...(x) t_{a_3}>. The labels are therefore not subspaces of F^{otimes3}, and the match with the next incoming labels A'(x)<t_{a_{j+1}}>(x)Q' only holds once Q=<t_{a_{j+1}}>(x)Q' is used. Likewise 'namely $P\otimes F$ of dimension $h$' should be P(x)F(x)Q (the dimension is unchanged). The paper carries Q throughout.
